request.spec:
When two people have the same momentum, break the tie by the higher alpha instead of by name.
The person with the higher alpha gets the better (lower) rank.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for this implementation's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
When two people have the same momentum, break the tie by the higher alpha instead of by name.
The person with the higher alpha gets the better (lower) rank.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
When two people have the same momentum, the one with the higher alpha now gets the better rank. Name is only used if alpha is also equal. `bin/e2e` passes.

The change is one line in the ranking order in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/people/PersonController.java`. Ranks are worked out on the server, so the front end needed no logic change. Anything else that uses rank, such as the sheet's leader and the percentiles, follows the new order automatically. No stored data or seed changes were needed.

Anyone with a momentum always has an alpha, but the code still puts people without an alpha last, just in case.

I also updated the comments that described the old name-based tie-break, in that file and in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`.
